title: A note on Γ-supercyclicity of dissipative composition operators
verdict: PASS — exact arbitrary-scalar equivalence in the stated separable setting

initial.phase: root read full controlling TeX before checking source bodies; the adversary independently sealed prior to any cited mathematics
initial.scope: For dissipative invertible composition operators on separable L^p, 1<=p<infinity, with uniform two-sided bounded distortion, scalar associated bilateral shift and composition operator have the same Gamma-supercyclic scalar sets for every arbitrary subset Gamma of C.
initial.proof: Necessity obtains two tails with the same allowed scalar at late times. Finitely many early projective lines are closed nowhere dense; unbounded-above x support supplies a fixed nonzero k, and the bounded left translation transfers tail weight from k to each j in the prescribed block. Sufficiency uses disjoint finite block perturbations along same n and lambda, continuity and Baire on the separable vector-valued space. The sequence-space measure model J uses locally equivalent measures with uniform level comparison and measurable representative gluing. The isometry D has inverse weight ratio and satisfies DB_w=SD. The alternative weighted translation argument has finite positive product obstruction to small times. A dense-range scalar functional or dense-range mixing transfer handles Gamma by continuity.
initial.boundary: No Gamma regularity. Sigma-finite measure does not imply separability; nonseparable product example with c_j=2^{-|j|} separates. Full vector-valued certified model and amplification, not bare factor map or scalar conjugacy.

math: A dense scalar Γ-orbit implies late returns after excluding early projective lines. Approximate a finite block with one λ and use a fixed nonzero high coordinate plus the bounded translation to force the second tail. A two-window finite-support perturbation with the same allowed λ, followed by a countable-base Baire argument, gives vector-valued amplification. The reverse follows from a nonzero functional. Bounded distortion matches the level measures uniformly to the base, enabling a bounded bijective J and the precise intertwining. The isometry D checks the scalar shift weights. A nonseparable Bernoulli product makes every orbit lie in a proper separable closed span although the scalar shift admits both tails.

peer.finding: Verified both same-scalar tails, independent Baire and measure argument, source scope and Abbar–Kuznetsova hypotheses. Bare factor with bounded right inverse fails control S⊕I→S; proof does not rely on it. Abbar general printed Theorem 2 omits separability, which the native theorem keeps and proves using a direct Baire step.
